Antiquity

an-TIK-wi-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Antiquity is the ancient past; great age.

The diver's flashlight swept across pottery from antiquity, still resting exactly where a storm had sunk the merchant ship.

Worked Example

Scholars of antiquity spend their careers studying the languages, laws, and myths of civilizations like ancient Greece, Rome, and Egypt.

Antiquity refers broadly to the distant historical past, especially the ancient civilizations of the Mediterranean and Near East.

How Antiquity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

antiqueness

antiqueness: the quality of being very old

the ancients

the ancients: people who lived in ancient times

Antonyms

modernity

modernity: the quality of being modern or up to date

novelty

novelty: the quality of being new and unusual

How Strong Is It? — age → prehistory → antiquity

age vs. antiquity

age vs. antiquity: Age simply describes how long something has existed, without specifically pointing to the ancient, historical past the way antiquity does.

prehistory vs. antiquity

prehistory vs. antiquity: Prehistory reaches back even further than antiquity, describing the vast stretch of time before any written records existed.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — antiqu-

root — antiqu-: old, ancient (Latin antiquus)

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state of, quality of (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Antiquity comes from Latin antiquus ('old, ancient'), the same root behind the everyday word antique, plus -ity -- 'the state of being ancient,' extended to mean the ancient past itself.

Use the root in a new word: antique

Use the root in a new word: antique: The dealer specialized in antique furniture, some pieces over two hundred years old.

Word Choice
